1.why: Hydrostatic pressure increases directly with water depth h.

wrong.a: Density of water does not change with depth here.
wrong.d: Pressure grows with depth, not decreases.

2.why: p = ρ × g × h, where ρ is fluid density and h is depth.

wrong.b: Mass is not in the hydrostatic pressure formula.
wrong.c: Area is for surface pressure, not fluid depth pressure.
wrong.d: Time is not part of this equation.

3.why: Restoring forests and drainage reduces flash flood risks.

wrong.a: Clearing more forests increases runoff and risks.
wrong.b: Building homes in riverbeds increases danger.
wrong.d: Ignoring weather warnings leads to more disasters.

_quiz_pool.question: If water depth doubles, what happens to the hydrostatic pressure p?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Pressure grows in direct step with depth h.

_quiz_pool.question: In p = ρ × g × h, what does ρ stand for?
_quiz_pool.explanation: ρ represents the density of the fluid.

_quiz_pool.question: Which measure helps reduce flash flood risks?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Healthy ecosystems and clear drainage reduce flood hazards.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of pressure p?
What is the acceleration due to gravity g used in physics calculations?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Standard gravity near Earth's surface is about 9.8 m/s².

_quiz_pool.question: Why must flood barriers be stronger at the bottom?
options: Water pressure is greatest at the deepest point
Water is colder at the bottom
_quiz_pool.explanation: Pressure increases with depth, so forces are highest at the base.

must_show: a plastic bottle with multiple holes at different heights
tape covering the holes while filling with water
water squirting out when tape is removed
safety: no flame, no hot water, no electricity
_lab_rubric.pass_if: The photos show the bottle setup and demonstrate that lower holes squirt water further due to higher pressure.

story.body_1: Monsoon rains and atmospheric waves bring heavy downpours to Sumatra and Java [1]. Swelling runoff overflows rapidly, submerging roads and homes in regions like Aceh [1].
story.body_2: Experts note that fragile ecosystems and burned soils worsen flood risks [1]. Restoring forests and improving river drainage help reduce disaster impacts [1].

timeline.2.text: Runoff swells and overflows banks rapidly.
timeline.3.text: Floodwaters exert intense pressure on structures.
physics.title: Pressure in a fluid
physics.body_1: When water rises during floods, depth increases. Deeper water presses down with greater force because of gravity and fluid density.
physics.body_2: Fluid pressure depends on three factors: water density ρ, gravity g, and depth h. Every extra metre adds more pressure.
physics.assumptions: We assume water density is uniform and ignore atmospheric pressure variation.
table.note: Pressure increases in direct proportion to water depth.

physics.tip: Deeper water means higher pressure. That is why flood barriers must be extra strong at the bottom.

lab.title: Water bottle pressure test
lab.step_1: Poke three small holes at different heights on a plastic water bottle.
lab.step_2: Fill the bottle with water while keeping the holes covered with tape.
lab.step_3: Remove the tape and observe how far the water squirts from each hole.
lab.question: Which hole squirted water the furthest and why?
